issues.legal_issue: A levy imposed as a fee is invalid when its proceeds are merged into general state revenues rather than earmarked for the purpose of the levy.
material_facts: A company executed a debenture trust deed secured by a mortgage and presented it for registration.
The registration authority demanded and collected a registration fee under a notification.
It was undisputed that the fee collected under the notification formed part of the general revenues of the State.
issues.conclusion: The fee was an illegal levy because its proceeds formed part of general state revenues; the notification was properly quashed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A valid fee requires both an element of quid pro quo, meaning that the authority renders some service in return, and that the amount collected be spent for the purpose of the levy rather than merged into general state revenues. The Court applied Mahant Sri Jagannath Ramanuj Das v. State of Orissa, Ratilal Panachand Gandhi v. State of Bombay, and State of Maharashtra v. The Salvation Army, Western India Territory.

predicates.fee_levied: An authority charged and collected a payment as a fee.
predicates.proceeds_merged_into_general_revenue: The authority placed the collected proceeds in general state revenues rather than earmarking them for the purpose of the fee.

issues.definition: When an authority collects a payment as a fee and places the proceeds in general state revenues, the fee levy is invalid.
